topic: JetGas / Port of Tallinn (Muuga) development and bioLNG focus
wiki_text: On 18 November 2024 the Port of Tallinn (Tallinna Sadam) signed a superficies-right agreement (~7,000 m2, 30-year term) with JetGas OÜ to develop a liquefied-methane terminal in Muuga Harbour. JetGas plans up to five storage tanks built in stages, with the first stage (one tank) targeted for end-2027 and full build-out by 2030. The facility is intended primarily for bioLNG and other methane fuels imported in larger consignments; no new investment is required from the port. GEM records OriginalPlannedStartYear=LatestPlannedStartYear=2030 (full project); the first-stage 2027 date is noted here. NB: GEM lists Liwathon E.O.S. as operator (from GIE), which is not corroborated by the 2024 Port of Tallinn/JetGas agreement (already flagged in GEM ResearcherNotes).

The regional FSRU serving Estonia and Finland is Excelerate Energy's 'Exemplar' (150,900 cbm, >5 bcm/y), moored at Inkoo, Finland (commissioning cargo Dec 2022). Estonia abandoned plans to take an equity stake in the Finnish (Gasgrid subsidiary) terminal and instead purchased the Paldiski mooring quay from Alexela and Infortar, with state stockpiling agency ESPA as owner; Paldiski serves as a reception-ready backup berth linked to the Balticconnector pipeline. Regional gas security is assessed jointly by the Estonian, Latvian and Finnish TSOs based on the Inkoo and Klaipėda FSRUs plus Latvian (Inčukalns) storage.
